newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks give back most gains at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks give back most gains at close.

text.p: Argentine stocks surrendered most gains at the close Wednesday as momentum fizzled following a brief wave of short-covering, dealers said.

"The market turned bullish late yesterday, but it soon hit resistance levels," said Jorge Bonanno at Interfin brokers. "Today's early rise seemed exaggerated ahead of Friday's options expirations, and now the mood has turned volatile -- we should expect scant volume and erratic trading Thursday."
The blue-chip MerVal index slipped off a high of 620.4 to close at 614.78, showing a gain of 0.3 percent.
The MerVal, which jumped 2.1 percent Tuesday, had shed 4.3 percent last week on the back of a shakeout on Wall Street.
"Obviously investors are still wary although the U.S. Federal Reserve's lack of action on interest rates (Tuesday) has underpinned the market," another trader said.

Analysts said new industrial production data released Wednesday by private consultants FIEL, who estimated year-on-year growth of 13.2 percent in November but saw a drop of 1.9 percent since October, dictated caution.
"We may be hitting a growth plateau which could potentially rattle some sectors of the market," said Bonanno.
The broad market ended up 0.8 percent in the session, with winners beating losers 37 to 15 and 22 stocks closing flat.
Floor turnover swelled to 23.3 million pesos from 14.5 million Tuesday, while over-the-counter volume remained hefty at 146.5 million pesos against 142.6 million Tuesday.

Top MerVal risers were oil firm Sol Petroleo, construction stock Juan Minetti and Banco de Galicia, up 3.7 percent, 2.3 percent and 2.0 percent, respectively. Losers were led by pulp and paper maker Celulosa, carmaker Sevel and foods giant Molinos, off 3.5 percent, 2.8 percent and 2.1 percent each.
